title: Derivative headroom + credit bank autoscaler with per-fleet safety curtains
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid autoscaler that blends a derivative-based headroom controller with a tenant-level burst credit bank and fleet-level safety curtains. Goal: provide predictable throughput guarantees while allowing safe microburst absorption and minimizing unnecessary scale-ups that increase cost. This ticket covers scoring/target metrics, control algorithms, credit accounting, coordination surface for fleet controllers, safety limits (ramp, absolute caps, cooldown), and observability hooks for rollback and forensic analysis.
background: Current autoscaler reacts to smoothed throughput/latency signals and often overprovisions for short-lived microbursts or under-reacts for rising slope-of-requests. We need an algorithm that anticipates direction changes (derivative), credits short bursts against recent idle capacity, and enforces hard/soft curtains to avoid tenant storms or fleet ramp explosions. This work builds on prior headroom and surge-buffered designs but introduces an explicit credit bank and a derivative term tuned for tokenized request bursts common to LLM workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler computes per-tenant target capacity using a combined metric: weighted(p95_latency, throughput, gpu_util, queue_depth, derivative_of_throughput)
Credit bank logic awards credits during sustained below-target utilization and debits during microbursts; credits expire after configurable TTL
Fleet safety curtains enforce per-pool soft caps and absolute hard caps; soft caps allow temporary overshoot charged to credit bank; hard caps block scale actions with clear telemetry
Max ramp rate enforced: no more than 2x capacity within 10 minutes unless emergency mode enabled by operator
End-to-end test harness demonstrates: handling of 10x traffic spike (60s) with credits vs. without credits, and controlled rollback on detected QoS regressions
Monitoring dashboards surface headroom, credit balances, recent derivative signals, last scaling decision, and reason codes for each scale action
tasks: Write design doc describing metric composition and credit accounting (Confluence)
Prototype derivative controller in the autoscaler service and run synthetic workload experiments
Implement credit bank module with persistence and eviction policy
Extend fleet controller to support soft/hard safety curtains and expose operator controls
Add telemetry: credit_balance, derivative_signal, proposed_capacity, final_capacity, reason_code
Create chaos test and benchmark comparing P95 and cost delta vs. existing autoscaler
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting with runtime and infra; agreed on metrics to track (p95_latency, throughput_delta/s, gpu_util, queue_depth). Assigned prototype owner and SLO targets.
2026-02-22: Early prototype of derivative term completed; synthetic generator shows earlier scale-ups for rising slope of requests with fewer false positives on jittery traffic.
2026-02-28: Design doc v0.1 posted to Confluence (link below). Decision: credits expire after 15m by default and are tenant-scoped with optional fleet pooling.

2026-03-03: First integration test failed: race between credit debit and concurrent scale decision produced transient over-allocations. Added conditional compare-and-swap on credit update and enqueued scale decisions to serialize per-tenant decisions.
2026-03-05: Implemented soft-curtain enforcement and telemetry emitters. Preparing A/B harness vs current autoscaler next week.

SRE (Natalie Kim) - 2026-03-01: Need emergency kill switch that disables credit spending and reverts to hard caps if fleet error budget drains below threshold.

Reviewer (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-05: Suggest adding metric for 'credit-induced_scale_actions' so we can evaluate cost tradeoffs over 30/90 days.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Aggressive derivative tuning reduces tail latency for rising traffic but increases sensitivity to measurement noise; mitigated by EWMA smoothing and minimum decision horizon
Tradeoff: Tenant credit banks reduce churn but can be gamed by tenants; addressed via TTL, rate limits on credit accrual, and audit logs
Tradeoff: Soft curtains improve availability at cost of temporary overprovisioning; operators can opt into strict hard caps for cost-sensitive fleets
qa_plan: Unit tests for credit bank arithmetic and expiry
Integration tests: serialized scale decisions under concurrent traffic patterns
Chaos tests: etcd partition recovery and credit reconciliation
Performance tests: measure cost delta and p95 improvements across 24h simulated workload
